title: How can a ruler and a set square draw a parallel line?
description: A line l and a point are drawn. A set square is placed along l, a ruler is held against it, and the set square slides along the ruler to the point. A line drawn there is checked by the equal corresponding angles it makes with the ruler.
teaching_notes: One idea: a set square that slides along a fixed ruler without turning keeps its angle with the ruler, so the new line is parallel to the old one. Watch for students who slide the set square and the ruler together.

source: Figure it Out (drawing parallel lines), Q1
video_script.why: The child uses the sliding set square of the solved example to draw a parallel line through a given point.
video_script.substitution: the book's own line l and point A, with the ruler, set square and pencil of a geometry box
video_script.anchor: a line l, a point A above it, a ruler, a set square and a pencil
video_script.payoff_line: The set square slides without turning, so the new line is parallel to l

final_answer.value: Slide the set square along a ruler until its side reaches A and draw along it; the line through A is parallel to l
final_answer.spoken: slide the set square along a ruler until its side reaches eigh and draw along it, and the line through eigh is parallel to l

hold_back: the line through A is parallel to l
maths_rules: place one side of the set square along l
hold the ruler against another side so that the ruler does not move
slide the set square along the ruler until the side that was along l reaches A, then draw along that side
the set square did not turn, so it makes the same angle with the ruler both times
with the ruler as the transversal, those two angles are corresponding angles, and they are equal, so the new line is parallel to l
video_script.design: One line l, one point A, a ruler and a set square drawn in two positions: first along l, then at A. The two equal angles with the ruler are marked in one colour.
